newsitem.title: USA: CBS, NBC tie for first in weekly TV ratings.
newsitem.headline: CBS, NBC tie for first in weekly TV ratings.

text.p: CBS, a Westinghouse Corp unit, and NBC, a General Electric Co unit, tied for first spot in U.S. television prime-time audience ratings for the week ending April 6, Neilsen Media Research said Tuesday.
Walt Disney Co's ABC network was second while FOX, a network owned by News Corp Ltd, was third.
UPN, a unit of Viacom Inc was fourth while WB, the television unit of Time Warner Inc, was fifth.

CBS's coverage of the National Collegiate Atheletic Association's basketball championships, in which Arizona beat Kentucky, ranked No. 1 among prime time shows during the week. The game garnered an 18.9 rating and a 31 percent share.
The network's pre-game show ranked 8th,, with a 13.3 rating and a 21 percent share. Tying at 8th was the CBS newsmagazine 60 Minutes, which, however had a bigger share at 25 percent.

NBC's sitcoms Seinfeld, Naked Truth and Friends came in second, third and fourth. Sienfeld had an 18.5 rating and a 30 percent share; Naked Truth, 15.3 and 30 percent; and Friends, 14.5 and 25 percent share.
E.R., an NBC dramatic series, tied with Friends at fourth, registering a 14.5 rating and 25 percent share.
Home Improvement, an ABC sitcom, and a Naked Truth Special were neck and neck at 6th, posting a 14.1 rating and shares of 22 percent and 23 percent, respectively.
Bringing up the rear for the week's top prime time shows was the Tuesday airing of NBC's Dateline newsmagazine, which garnered a 12.5 rating and 22 percent market share.
